bull_bear.body: No dividend/buyback specifics this call (Page is a historically high-dividend payer). FY29 Rs.8,000cr target to be funded organically + inorganic optionality (new channels/QC, international/GCC, possible new licenses/brands/acquisitions — evaluated opportunistically). Working capital tight (NWC 52 days).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Demand:** Persistent soft/selective consumer sentiment; entry-level/mass + general-trade most exposed; like-to-like throughput per GT store softened.
- **Channel disruption:** Offline→online and unorganized→organized shift stresses GT/MBO; retailer-level stock corrections dampening reported growth.
- **Competition:** A competitor reported "strong double-digit growth"; multiple new athleisure entrants. Mgmt denies share loss (no syndicated data; claims gains in e-comm/LFS/partner where measured) — but the +2% 9M volume vs faster-growing industry raises a market-share question flagged by analysts (Citi).
- **Input cost / one-offs:** Cotton/yarn & textile-export/FTA volatility; future labour-code rules; recurring possibility of provisions.
- **Margin normalization:** Current 22–23% EBITDA to step down to 19–21% as investment ramps.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Measured, defensive-confident. Repeatedly deflected double-digit-growth timeline ("too many variables") while insisting headroom/penetration intact and recovery "steady." Firmly resisted market-share-loss narrative ("I'll be the first to admit if there is… we have evidence to the contrary"). Disciplined on pricing (no hikes in 3–4 yrs, value-for-money philosophy). Confident on new products (Bonded, Groove) and international.
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Channel-mix mechanics on ASP:** jockey.in + marketplaces realize **MRP as revenue**, so any offline→online shift mechanically lifts value growth vs volume — part of the +4% realization is a channel-accounting effect, not pure premiumization.
- Insourcing fell to 64% (from 70%); higher outsourcing is a deliberate cost lever and partly explains lower headcount + inventory.
- GST cut (12%→5%) only touched a small slice (athleisure/outerwear >Rs.1,000); ~all innerwear stayed at 5% — negligible brand impact; passed on where selling price carried 12%.
- ASP uplift also helped by winter seasonality (higher-priced hoodies/jackets) + Bonded (highest-priced range ever) — partly transient.
- GT under-penetration of portfolio (carries far fewer styles than EBOs) is "not by design" — flagged as self-help growth lever independent of consumer recovery.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- "Investing in future, through strong internal accruals and generating high ROCE" — the deck frames reinvestment as internally funded, with "Strong Balance Sheet" and "Robust Financials" listed among key strengths.
- Return metrics are stated inconsistently: the "At a Glance" slide says "Healthy ROCE 70.9%", the Key Strengths slide says "Robust Financials with ROCE of 73%", and the balance-sheet slide shows FY26 ROCE 73.
- Shareholding as on June 2026: Promoters 42.89%, Mutual Funds 23.70%, FPI 18.91%, Insurance Companies and Other DIIs 5.69%, Others (incl. SWF, pension funds) 8.81%; Market Cap ~INR 462 bn as on June 2026.
- The deck shows an EPS and DPS (₹) chart and a working-capital-days chart across FY22-FY26, but in this extraction the values are not reliably bound to their years or series, so no per-year EPS, DPS or working-capital figure is asserted here.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Exclusive, long-standing brand licenses: sole JOCKEY licensee across 12 countries and sole Indian licensee of Speedo
- Strong in-house manufacturing capabilities combined with strategic outsourcing (integrated manufacturing approach)
- Extensive distribution network: 1,579 Exclusive Business Outlets, 1,15,644 retail touchpoints, and presence across 893 Large Format Stores for JOCKEY; 36 EBOs and 962 MBOs for Speedo
- High brand equity - JOCKEY Awareness Score of 96% and Most Preferred Brand Score of 60% among target audience
- Distribution management system modernised in collaboration with Salesforce and Wonder Soft, improving product availability and accessibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intensifying competition from international apparel brands — Increasing entry and expansion of international apparel brands in India, attracted by the country's potential to become one of the largest apparel markets globally, may intensify competition, per the MD&A's stated long-term industry threats.
- D2C startup competition and discounting pressure — The rapid emergence of Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) startups in the innerwear and athleisure segments, often leveraging aggressive discounting strategies, poses pricing and customer acquisition challenges, per the MD&A's stated threats.
- Single business segment concentration — The Company operates in a single business segment - the manufacturing and sale of garments - with no separate reportable segments, meaning the entire business is exposed to demand and competitive dynamics in one category.
- Enterprise risk spans strategic, compliance, operational, reporting and EHS categories — The Company's SCORE risk framework identifies Strategic Risks, Compliance Risks, Operational Risks, Reporting obligations and Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Risks as the categories it systematically monitors and mitigates, indicating these are the areas management itself flags as material to the business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Consumer demand "selective"/"weak" through Q1–Q2, some uplift in Q3, expected to flow into Q4. Q1/Q2 hurt by geopolitical disruption + floods keeping retail shut. General-trade/MBO channel softest; LFS & EBO flattish like-to-like; like-to-like at consumer level not de-grown but "a lot softer than targeted." Men's innerwear (largest base) toughest; women's innerwear & outerwear/athleisure better in both volume & value.
business.title: Demand commentary

business.body:
- **Men's innerwear:** Largest base, **relatively toughest**; entry-level/economy weakest. Bonded Collection (men's innerwear, Sep/Oct launch) = highest-priced product yet, very well received.
- **Women's innerwear:** Better volume + value growth; new Bonded bras = top-priced, strong uptake — lifting ASP.
- **Athleisure / outerwear:** Outperforming; winter products (sweatshirts/hoodies/jackets) drove ASP. JKY Groove (athleisure collection, summer'25 Q1 + winter Q3) scaling EBO reach; success "heartening."
- **Speedo / swimwear:** Not discussed on this call.
business.title: Segment performance

business.body:
- Page's GT/entry-level weakness + competitor double-digit growth + new athleisure entrants → potential read-through beneficiaries: mass/value innerwear peers and quick-commerce-native apparel players capturing the offline→online shift. (No specific listed beneficiary named by mgmt; ✅/⭐ left empty — inference only.)

(USA) for manufacture, distribution and marketing of the JOCKEY brand in India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Oman, Qatar, Maldives, Bhutan, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Bahrain; also exclusive licensee of Speedo (Pentland Group / Speedo International Ltd., Nottingham UK) for India. Deck lists the licence tenure as "License with Jockey International till 2040".
- Jockey is described as the flagship brand and "a market leader in the premium innerwear and athleisure category", and as "one of the world's most loved and recognizable brands, with a presence in over 140 countries".
- Distribution reach (Jockey): 2,732 cities & towns, 1,15,208 Multi Brand Outlets, 1,604 Exclusive Brand Stores, 930 Large Format Stores, plus online; the "At a Glance" slide instead states 1,15,871 Retail Network and 1,640 Exclusive Brand Stores with 930 Large Format Stores (both readings appear in the deck).
- Speedo is available in 663 stores and 36 EBOs spread across 150+ cities as well as online (market-coverage slide: 663 stores/150 cities, 36 stores/11 cities).
- Channel structure spans Multi-Brand Trade (3,989 Distributor Accounts, 759 team strength), Exclusive Brand Stores (incl. 29 Exclusive Woman Stores, 33 Exclusive Juniors Stores, 35 Factory Outlets across 589 cities/towns), Key Department Stores (15 partner chains, 930 stores, 1,390 points of sale) and E-Commerce (Jockey.in, Speedo.in and partners).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Sustainability target] The sustainability "Outcomes" slide states economic performance of "Rs 4,934 Cr" sustainable revenue growth with a "Target: Rs. 8000 Cr by FY 28" — this sits alongside, and is labelled differently from, the FY26 revenue of ₹52,468 mn on the financial-performance slide.
- [Awards] "Licensee of the Decade" award from Jockey International for the second consecutive time, conferred during Jockey's 150th anniversary year; also WSO Gold 4 Star Workplace OHS&E award, ABK AOTS 5S and Kaizen awards, CII silver trophy (Unit 12, 17th National POKA YOKE competition), IGBC Platinum green-building certification at Unit 22, and WRAP certification.
- [Logistics] Management notes "short-term logistics disruptions during the period meant that demand could not be serviced as fully as we would have liked", so underlying volume growth did not fully translate into reported revenue growth; conditions are described as having begun to settle and temporary in nature.
- [Brand reach] Social/digital following disclosed as 18,01,100 / 4,24,900 / 22,576 / 42,500 on one slide and 3,82,000 / 26,900 / 1,870 on another; the platform names are not recoverable from this extraction, so the followers are not attributed to specific channels.

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body:
- GM ~58%, down ~200bps QoQ (product-cost variation + higher marketing spend + slight employee-cost rise). GM expected "largely stable" going forward, near lifetime highs.
- Productivity lever: recruitment freeze most of the year, lean/automation/value-stream-mapping cut headcount by ~2,500–3,000; staff cost well within target — key to defending margins in a soft top line. Odisha (Orissa) facility added workforce per plan; no incentive income in ASP.
- Cotton/yarn: stable input costs this quarter; mgmt watching cotton prices, FTAs and textile-export developments — flagged as volatile risk to input costs.
- Higher outsourcing (now ~36% vs ~30%) gave product-cost benefits.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q3FY26 (this call):** Rev +5.6% / Vol +1.4% / EBITDA margin 22.9% / PAT -7.4% reported (one-off Rs.350mn labour-code provision; ex-one-off broadly flat). ASP +4% (mix-only, no price hike). GM ~58% (-200bps QoQ). EBITDA band reaffirmed 19–21% (FY26 & FY27); current ~22–23% called unsustainable. Double-digit VOLUME growth aspired, no timeline; Q4 ≥ Q3. JKY Groove 150→~500 EBOs by Apr-26. Full GCC license (added Saudi/Kuwait/Bahrain). FY29 Rs.8,000cr target reaffirmed. Insourcing 64% (from 70%). Headcount cut ~2,500–3,000 (recruitment freeze + automation).
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume growth:** Aspires to return to **double-digit VOLUME growth** (CEO explicit when pressed: intent is double-digit volume, the decade-long track record), but **NO timeline given** — "difficult to put a timeline"; not committed for FY26; Q4 expected better than Q3 ("better Q3 to flow into Q4").
- **Value growth:** Q3 value +5.6% on +1.4% volume = ASP-led; +4% realization from mix only.
- **EBITDA margin:** Reaffirmed long-term band **19–21%** for FY26 AND FY27. Current ~22–23% explicitly called **NOT sustainable** — will normalize to 19–21% as brand/marketing/automation investment steps up. Mgmt "not chasing a % EBITDA" — prefers absolute margin growth via value-for-money, won't outprice consumers.
- **ASP:** No price hike taken in 3–4 years; "considering" hikes only if input-cost inflation (cotton/yarn, FTA/export-driven) exceeds what can be absorbed. None hit market yet.
- **Distribution / QC:** Network at 1,13,600 MBOs, 1,556 EBOs, 1,778 LFS. JKY Groove athleisure: 50 EBOs (Q1) → 150 EBOs (Q3) → target ~500 EBOs by Apr-2026 (summer'26 launch). Quick-commerce/e-commerce strong growth, leads e-comm platforms.
- **Long-term target:** **Rs. 8,000 cr revenue by FY29** reaffirmed (organic + inorganic optionality).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **Athleisure:** JKY Groove collection (not yet a brand — could become sub-brand) scaling 150→~500 EBOs by Apr-26; selectively extended to general trade in metros. 1–2 more "new product spaces" being toyed with; at least one to launch in FY27.
- **Women's:** Bonded bras premium range gaining.
- **Quick-commerce:** Rising salience; entry-level/economy portfolio suits QC & e-comm — channel shift partly explains GT weakness; flagged as inorganic growth avenue.
- **ASP/premiumization:** Mid-premium & premium clearly outperform entry-level; most new/innovative launches priced at premium; key value-growth driver.
- **International:** Full GCC Jockey license now (added Saudi, Kuwait, Bahrain to UAE/Oman/Qatar) — "much larger" market, launch "soon"; taken "very seriously" for FY27. Inorganic optionality (acquisitions/new licenses) open but no visibility.
outlook.title: Growth & optionality

outlook.body:
- Scaling up manufacturing and sales capacities to meet growing demand
- Expanding channel presence across distribution networks, exclusive brand outlets, large format stores, and e-commerce platforms
- Increasing investments in sales and marketing, including point-of-sale visibility and traditional/digital advertising
- Strengthening focus on research and development, product innovation, automation, and digital transformation to enhance operational efficiency and customer experience
- Balanced manufacturing capacity approach combining in-house expansion and strategic outsourcing, supported by long-standing vendor partnerships, technology-led operations and strong quality systems
- Continued digital transformation via SAP S/4HANA, Salesforce Distribution Management System, and a new Human Resource Management System to build a scalable, data-driven, agile operating model
- Strengthening D2C segment through the Consumer Data Platform, enhanced marketing technology capabilities, and expansion of dark store infrastructure
- Disciplined capital allocation balancing investments in growth, manufacturing capacity, and technology with shareholder returns
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26, the Company strengthened its manufacturing footprint with the successful inauguration of two new facilities at K.R. Pete, Karnataka and Cuttack, Odisha; both have commenced garment production and are progressively scaling up capacity, with the Cuttack facility also initiating production of socks and elastic. Capacity expansion continued to advance: a K.R. Pete Phase 2 expansion of approximately 1 lakh sq. ft. of built-up area (planned to house elastic manufacturing capabilities) is scheduled for handover by Q2 FY27, and the Company has initiated plans for a new innerwear manufacturing facility in Odisha-Khordha (about 30 km from the existing project site) expected to become operational by FY2028-29. Manufacturing capacity building follows a balanced approach combining in-house expansion with strategic outsourcing (including Outsourcing Garmenting Vendors), supported by long-standing vendor partnerships. The Company is also evaluating the establishment of Regional Distribution Centres (RDCs) in the Eastern and Western regions to strengthen geographic reach and service responsiveness.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's Textile & Apparel market estimated at US$194 billion in FY2025-26 with domestic market growing at ~7% CAGR, providing a long-term structural growth opportunity for organized innerwear, athleisure and active lifestyle categories
- Rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanization, premiumization trends, growing brand consciousness and rapid formalization of the retail ecosystem expected to support long-term category expansion and penetration across online and offline channels
- Encouraging consumer response to premium and differentiated product offerings, including the new JKY Groove range targeted at Gen Z consumers and bonding-technology products, seen as an emerging premiumisation contributor
- E-commerce channel continuing strong growth trajectory, with further D2C strengthening expected to support demand
- Inflationary pressures, particularly in cotton and other key raw materials, persisted but were mitigated through strategic sourcing, supply chain optimization, production efficiencies and disciplined cost management, keeping EBITDA margins within the planned 19-21% operating framework
- Near-term uncertainty from geopolitical developments (including the Middle East conflict) and macroeconomic factors including commodity price fluctuations and global trade realignments, against which management expresses cautious optimism given a strong balance sheet and robust supply chain
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Category leader navigating a soft, selective-demand cycle: holding margins via productivity/cost control and premium mix while volume growth stalls (+1.4% YoY) — value > volume on ASP/mix; double-digit volume growth deferred but framed as intact long-term, with FY29 Rs.8,000cr revenue target reaffirmed.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition from international apparel brands
risks.note: Increasing entry and expansion of international apparel brands in India, attracted by the country's potential to become one of the largest apparel markets globally, may intensify competition, per the MD&A's stated long-term industry threats.

risks.risk: D2C startup competition and discounting pressure
risks.note: The rapid emergence of Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) startups in the innerwear and athleisure segments, often leveraging aggressive discounting strategies, poses pricing and customer acquisition challenges, per the MD&A's stated threats.

The Company operates in a single business segment - the manufacturing and sale of garments - with no separate reportable segments, meaning the entire business is exposed to demand and competitive dynamics in one category.

risks.risk: Enterprise risk spans strategic, compliance, operational, reporting and EHS categories
risks.note: The Company's SCORE risk framework identifies Strategic Risks, Compliance Risks, Operational Risks, Reporting obligations and Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Risks as the categories it systematically monitors and mitigates, indicating these are the areas management itself flags as material to the business.

thesis (one line): Category leader navigating a soft, selective-demand cycle: holding margins via productivity/cost control and premium mix while volume growth stalls (+1.4% YoY) — value > volume on ASP/mix; double-digit volume growth deferred but framed as intact long-term, with FY29 Rs.8,000cr revenue target reaffirmed.
scorecard (q3 fy26, yoy):
| Metric | Q3FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Rs. 13,868 mn | +5.6% | Driven by ASP/mix, not price hikes |
| Sales volume | 58.6 mn pieces | +1.4% | Weak; entry-level/men's lagging |
| EBITDA | Rs. 3,181 mn | +5.2% | Margin 22.9% (above 19–21% guided band) |
| EBITDA margin | 22.9% | — | Elevated; mgmt says not sustainable, will revert to 19–21% |
| PBT (pre-exceptional) | Rs. 2,913 mn | +5.9% | Underlying profit healthy |
| PAT (reported) | Rs. 1,895 mn | **-7.4%** | Hit by one-off provision |
| PAT (normalized, ex one-off) | ~broadly in line with Q3FY25 | ~flat/low-single | Ex Rs.350mn provision, growth "broadly in line" with Q3FY25 |
| Gross margin | ~58% | — | Down ~200bps QoQ (from ~60%) on product cost + marketing/employee cost; near lifetime highs but softened seq. |
| ASP / net realization | +4% YoY | — | vs ~1% prior quarter; pure mix (category + channel), **zero price hike** |
| Working capital | NWC 52 days (vs 54 BoY); Inventory 67 days (vs 64 BoY) | — | Inventory days up slightly; insourcing 64% (vs 70% prior qtr), outsourcing ~36% |

**One-offs:** Rs. 350 mn exceptional provision for gratuity + earned leave from new direct labour wage codes (notified Nov-2025; changed wage definition / higher basic for retirement benefits). This is the sole driver of the PAT decline. No ESOP charge or inventory-correction one-off flagged this quarter. **9M FY26:** Revenue Rs. 39,942 mn (+4.1%), Volume 173.8 mn pcs (+1.9%), EBITDA Rs. 8,923 mn (+7.9%, margin 22.3%), PAT Rs. 5,851 mn (+3.5%).
guidance (critical):
- **Volume growth:** Aspires to return to **double-digit VOLUME growth** (CEO explicit when pressed: intent is double-digit volume, the decade-long track record), but **NO timeline given** — "difficult to put a timeline"; not committed for FY26; Q4 expected better than Q3 ("better Q3 to flow into Q4").
- **Value growth:** Q3 value +5.6% on +1.4% volume = ASP-led; +4% realization from mix only.
- **EBITDA margin:** Reaffirmed long-term band **19–21%** for FY26 AND FY27. Current ~22–23% explicitly called **NOT sustainable** — will normalize to 19–21% as brand/marketing/automation investment steps up. Mgmt "not chasing a % EBITDA" — prefers absolute margin growth via value-for-money, won't outprice consumers.
- **ASP:** No price hike taken in 3–4 years; "considering" hikes only if input-cost inflation (cotton/yarn, FTA/export-driven) exceeds what can be absorbed. None hit market yet.
- **Distribution / QC:** Network at 1,13,600 MBOs, 1,556 EBOs, 1,778 LFS. JKY Groove athleisure: 50 EBOs (Q1) → 150 EBOs (Q3) → target ~500 EBOs by Apr-2026 (summer'26 launch). Quick-commerce/e-commerce strong growth, leads e-comm platforms.
- **Long-term target:** **Rs. 8,000 cr revenue by FY29** reaffirmed (organic + inorganic optionality).
demand commentary: Consumer demand "selective"/"weak" through Q1–Q2, some uplift in Q3, expected to flow into Q4. Q1/Q2 hurt by geopolitical disruption + floods keeping retail shut. General-trade/MBO channel softest; LFS & EBO flattish like-to-like; like-to-like at consumer level not de-grown but "a lot softer than targeted." Men's innerwear (largest base) toughest; women's innerwear & outerwear/athleisure better in both volume & value.
segment performance:
- **Men's innerwear:** Largest base, **relatively toughest**; entry-level/economy weakest. Bonded Collection (men's innerwear, Sep/Oct launch) = highest-priced product yet, very well received.
- **Women's innerwear:** Better volume + value growth; new Bonded bras = top-priced, strong uptake — lifting ASP.
- **Athleisure / outerwear:** Outperforming; winter products (sweatshirts/hoodies/jackets) drove ASP. JKY Groove (athleisure collection, summer'25 Q1 + winter Q3) scaling EBO reach; success "heartening."
- **Speedo / swimwear:** Not discussed on this call.
growth & optionality:
- **Athleisure:** JKY Groove collection (not yet a brand — could become sub-brand) scaling 150→~500 EBOs by Apr-26; selectively extended to general trade in metros. 1–2 more "new product spaces" being toyed with; at least one to launch in FY27.
- **Women's:** Bonded bras premium range gaining.
- **Quick-commerce:** Rising salience; entry-level/economy portfolio suits QC & e-comm — channel shift partly explains GT weakness; flagged as inorganic growth avenue.
- **ASP/premiumization:** Mid-premium & premium clearly outperform entry-level; most new/innovative launches priced at premium; key value-growth driver.
- **International:** Full GCC Jockey license now (added Saudi, Kuwait, Bahrain to UAE/Oman/Qatar) — "much larger" market, launch "soon"; taken "very seriously" for FY27. Inorganic optionality (acquisitions/new licenses) open but no visibility.
margins & cost:
- GM ~58%, down ~200bps QoQ (product-cost variation + higher marketing spend + slight employee-cost rise). GM expected "largely stable" going forward, near lifetime highs.
- Productivity lever: recruitment freeze most of the year, lean/automation/value-stream-mapping cut headcount by ~2,500–3,000; staff cost well within target — key to defending margins in a soft top line. Odisha (Orissa) facility added workforce per plan; no incentive income in ASP.
- Cotton/yarn: stable input costs this quarter; mgmt watching cotton prices, FTAs and textile-export developments — flagged as volatile risk to input costs.
- Higher outsourcing (now ~36% vs ~30%) gave product-cost benefits.
capex: No explicit capex number this call. Odisha/Orissa manufacturing facility ramped per plan (new-facility headcount addition). Ongoing investment in automation/lean and store renovations (Q4 typically renovation-heavy for new retail identity).
capital allocation: No dividend/buyback specifics this call (Page is a historically high-dividend payer). FY29 Rs.8,000cr target to be funded organically + inorganic optionality (new channels/QC, international/GCC, possible new licenses/brands/acquisitions — evaluated opportunistically). Working capital tight (NWC 52 days).
risks:
- **Demand:** Persistent soft/selective consumer sentiment; entry-level/mass + general-trade most exposed; like-to-like throughput per GT store softened.
- **Channel disruption:** Offline→online and unorganized→organized shift stresses GT/MBO; retailer-level stock corrections dampening reported growth.
- **Competition:** A competitor reported "strong double-digit growth"; multiple new athleisure entrants. Mgmt denies share loss (no syndicated data; claims gains in e-comm/LFS/partner where measured) — but the +2% 9M volume vs faster-growing industry raises a market-share question flagged by analysts (Citi).
- **Input cost / one-offs:** Cotton/yarn & textile-export/FTA volatility; future labour-code rules; recurring possibility of provisions.
- **Margin normalization:** Current 22–23% EBITDA to step down to 19–21% as investment ramps.
management tone: Measured, defensive-confident. Repeatedly deflected double-digit-growth timeline ("too many variables") while insisting headroom/penetration intact and recovery "steady." Firmly resisted market-share-loss narrative ("I'll be the first to admit if there is… we have evidence to the contrary"). Disciplined on pricing (no hikes in 3–4 yrs, value-for-money philosophy). Confident on new products (Bonded, Groove) and international.
non-obvious points:
- **Channel-mix mechanics on ASP:** jockey.in + marketplaces realize **MRP as revenue**, so any offline→online shift mechanically lifts value growth vs volume — part of the +4% realization is a channel-accounting effect, not pure premiumization.
- Insourcing fell to 64% (from 70%); higher outsourcing is a deliberate cost lever and partly explains lower headcount + inventory.
- GST cut (12%→5%) only touched a small slice (athleisure/outerwear >Rs.1,000); ~all innerwear stayed at 5% — negligible brand impact; passed on where selling price carried 12%.
- ASP uplift also helped by winter seasonality (higher-priced hoodies/jackets) + Bonded (highest-priced range ever) — partly transient.
- GT under-penetration of portfolio (carries far fewer styles than EBOs) is "not by design" — flagged as self-help growth lever independent of consumer recovery.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Page's GT/entry-level weakness + competitor double-digit growth + new athleisure entrants → potential read-through beneficiaries: mass/value innerwear peers and quick-commerce-native apparel players capturing the offline→online shift. (No specific listed beneficiary named by mgmt; ✅/⭐ left empty — inference only.)

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Page Industries Limited holds the exclusive license to manufacture, operate and market JOCKEY-branded innerwear, leisurewear and athleisure across India and ten neighbouring/Gulf countries, and is the exclusive Indian licensee of Speedo swimwear.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PIL holds the license for manufacturing, operations, and marketing of JOCKEY-branded products across India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Maldives, Bhutan, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain, and is the exclusive licensee of Speedo International Ltd. in India for manufacturing, marketing and distribution of Speedo-branded products. The Company operates in a single business segment - the manufacturing and sale of garments - with no separate reportable segments.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's Textile & Apparel market estimated at US$194 billion in FY2025-26 with domestic market growing at ~7% CAGR, providing a long-term structural growth opportunity for organized innerwear, athleisure and active lifestyle categories
- Rising disposable incomes, increasing urbanization, premiumization trends, growing brand consciousness and rapid formalization of the retail ecosystem expected to support long-term category expansion and penetration across online and offline channels
- Encouraging consumer response to premium and differentiated product offerings, including the new JKY Groove range targeted at Gen Z consumers and bonding-technology products, seen as an emerging premiumisation contributor
- E-commerce channel continuing strong growth trajectory, with further D2C strengthening expected to support demand
- Inflationary pressures, particularly in cotton and other key raw materials, persisted but were mitigated through strategic sourcing, supply chain optimization, production efficiencies and disciplined cost management, keeping EBITDA margins within the planned 19-21% operating framework
- Near-term uncertainty from geopolitical developments (including the Middle East conflict) and macroeconomic factors including commodity price fluctuations and global trade realignments, against which management expresses cautious optimism given a strong balance sheet and robust supply chain

| ASP / net realization | +4% YoY | — | vs ~1% prior quarter; pure mix (category + channel), **zero price hike** |
| Working capital | NWC 52 days (vs 54 BoY); Inventory 67 days (vs 64 BoY) | — | Inventory days up slightly; insourcing 64% (vs 70% prior qtr), outsourcing ~36% |

**One-offs:** Rs. 350 mn exceptional provision for gratuity + earned leave from new direct labour wage codes (notified Nov-2025; changed wage definition / higher basic for retirement benefits). This is the sole driver of the PAT decline. No ESOP charge or inventory-correction one-off flagged this quarter. **9M FY26:** Revenue Rs. 39,942 mn (+4.1%), Volume 173.8 mn pcs (+1.9%), EBITDA Rs. 8,923 mn (+7.9%, margin 22.3%), PAT Rs. 5,851 mn (+3.5%).
guidance (critical):
- **Volume growth:** Aspires to return to **double-digit VOLUME growth** (CEO explicit when pressed: intent is double-digit volume, the decade-long track record), but **NO timeline given** — "difficult to put a timeline"; not committed for FY26; Q4 expected better than Q3 ("better Q3 to flow into Q4").
- **Value growth:** Q3 value +5.6% on +1.4% volume = ASP-led; +4% realization from mix only.
- **EBITDA margin:** Reaffirmed long-term band **19–21%** for FY26 AND FY27. Current ~22–23% explicitly called **NOT sustainable** — will normalize to 19–21% as brand/marketing/automation investment steps up. Mgmt "not chasing a % EBITDA" — prefers absolute margin growth via value-for-money, won't outprice consumers.
- **ASP:** No price hike taken in 3–4 years; "considering" hikes only if input-cost inflation (cotton/yarn, FTA/export-driven) exceeds what can be absorbed. None hit market yet.
- **Distribution / QC:** Network at 1,13,600 MBOs, 1,556 EBOs, 1,778 LFS. JKY Groove athleisure: 50 EBOs (Q1) → 150 EBOs (Q3) → target ~500 EBOs by Apr-2026 (summer'26 launch). Quick-commerce/e-commerce strong growth, leads e-comm platforms.
- **Long-term target:** **Rs. 8,000 cr revenue by FY29** reaffirmed (organic + inorganic optionality).
demand commentary: Consumer demand "selective"/"weak" through Q1–Q2, some uplift in Q3, expected to flow into Q4. Q1/Q2 hurt by geopolitical disruption + floods keeping retail shut. General-trade/MBO channel softest; LFS & EBO flattish like-to-like; like-to-like at consumer level not de-grown but "a lot softer than targeted." Men's innerwear (largest base) toughest; women's innerwear & outerwear/athleisure better in both volume & value.
segment performance:
- **Men's innerwear:** Largest base, **relatively toughest**; entry-level/economy weakest. Bonded Collection (men's innerwear, Sep/Oct launch) = highest-priced product yet, very well received.
- **Women's innerwear:** Better volume + value growth; new Bonded bras = top-priced, strong uptake — lifting ASP.
- **Athleisure / outerwear:** Outperforming; winter products (sweatshirts/hoodies/jackets) drove ASP. JKY Groove (athleisure collection, summer'25 Q1 + winter Q3) scaling EBO reach; success "heartening."
- **Speedo / swimwear:** Not discussed on this call.
growth & optionality:
- **Athleisure:** JKY Groove collection (not yet a brand — could become sub-brand) scaling 150→~500 EBOs by Apr-26; selectively extended to general trade in metros. 1–2 more "new product spaces" being toyed with; at least one to launch in FY27.
- **Women's:** Bonded bras premium range gaining.
- **Quick-commerce:** Rising salience; entry-level/economy portfolio suits QC & e-comm — channel shift partly explains GT weakness; flagged as inorganic growth avenue.
- **ASP/premiumization:** Mid-premium & premium clearly outperform entry-level; most new/innovative launches priced at premium; key value-growth driver.
- **International:** Full GCC Jockey license now (added Saudi, Kuwait, Bahrain to UAE/Oman/Qatar) — "much larger" market, launch "soon"; taken "very seriously" for FY27. Inorganic optionality (acquisitions/new licenses) open but no visibility.
margins & cost:
- GM ~58%, down ~200bps QoQ (product-cost variation + higher marketing spend + slight employee-cost rise). GM expected "largely stable" going forward, near lifetime highs.
- Productivity lever: recruitment freeze most of the year, lean/automation/value-stream-mapping cut headcount by ~2,500–3,000; staff cost well within target — key to defending margins in a soft top line. Odisha (Orissa) facility added workforce per plan; no incentive income in ASP.
- Cotton/yarn: stable input costs this quarter; mgmt watching cotton prices, FTAs and textile-export developments — flagged as volatile risk to input costs.
- Higher outsourcing (now ~36% vs ~30%) gave product-cost benefits.
capex: No explicit capex number this call. Odisha/Orissa manufacturing facility ramped per plan (new-facility headcount addition). Ongoing investment in automation/lean and store renovations (Q4 typically renovation-heavy for new retail identity).
capital allocation: No dividend/buyback specifics this call (Page is a historically high-dividend payer). FY29 Rs.8,000cr target to be funded organically + inorganic optionality (new channels/QC, international/GCC, possible new licenses/brands/acquisitions — evaluated opportunistically). Working capital tight (NWC 52 days).
risks:
- **Demand:** Persistent soft/selective consumer sentiment; entry-level/mass + general-trade most exposed; like-to-like throughput per GT store softened.
- **Channel disruption:** Offline→online and unorganized→organized shift stresses GT/MBO; retailer-level stock corrections dampening reported growth.
- **Competition:** A competitor reported "strong double-digit growth"; multiple new athleisure entrants. Mgmt denies share loss (no syndicated data; claims gains in e-comm/LFS/partner where measured) — but the +2% 9M volume vs faster-growing industry raises a market-share question flagged by analysts (Citi).
- **Input cost / one-offs:** Cotton/yarn & textile-export/FTA volatility; future labour-code rules; recurring possibility of provisions.
- **Margin normalization:** Current 22–23% EBITDA to step down to 19–21% as investment ramps.
management tone: Measured, defensive-confident. Repeatedly deflected double-digit-growth timeline ("too many variables") while insisting headroom/penetration intact and recovery "steady." Firmly resisted market-share-loss narrative ("I'll be the first to admit if there is… we have evidence to the contrary"). Disciplined on pricing (no hikes in 3–4 yrs, value-for-money philosophy). Confident on new products (Bonded, Groove) and international.
non-obvious points:
- **Channel-mix mechanics on ASP:** jockey.in + marketplaces realize **MRP as revenue**, so any offline→online shift mechanically lifts value growth vs volume — part of the +4% realization is a channel-accounting effect, not pure premiumization.
- Insourcing fell to 64% (from 70%); higher outsourcing is a deliberate cost lever and partly explains lower headcount + inventory.
- GST cut (12%→5%) only touched a small slice (athleisure/outerwear >Rs.1,000); ~all innerwear stayed at 5% — negligible brand impact; passed on where selling price carried 12%.
- ASP uplift also helped by winter seasonality (higher-priced hoodies/jackets) + Bonded (highest-priced range ever) — partly transient.
- GT under-penetration of portfolio (carries far fewer styles than EBOs) is "not by design" — flagged as self-help growth lever independent of consumer recovery.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Page's GT/entry-level weakness + competitor double-digit growth + new athleisure entrants → potential read-through beneficiaries: mass/value innerwear peers and quick-commerce-native apparel players capturing the offline→online shift. (No specific listed beneficiary named by mgmt; ✅/⭐ left empty — inference only.)

---
qoq log: - **Q3FY26 (this call):** Rev +5.6% / Vol +1.4% / EBITDA margin 22.9% / PAT -7.4% reported (one-off Rs.350mn labour-code provision; ex-one-off broadly flat). ASP +4% (mix-only, no price hike). GM ~58% (-200bps QoQ). EBITDA band reaffirmed 19–21% (FY26 & FY27); current ~22–23% called unsustainable. Double-digit VOLUME growth aspired, no timeline; Q4 ≥ Q3. JKY Groove 150→~500 EBOs by Apr-26. Full GCC license (added Saudi/Kuwait/Bahrain). FY29 Rs.8,000cr target reaffirmed. Insourcing 64% (from 70%). Headcount cut ~2,500–3,000 (recruitment freeze + automation).

themes.title: Branded innerwear & domestic apparel
themes.need: Branded innerwear and domestic apparel are driven by rural recovery, GST 2.0 and distribution reach - a domestic-consumption thesis, not the China+1/FTA export tailwind powering exporters and synthetics.
themes.driver: Rural recovery + GST 2.0 demand pull and distribution-led volume growth.
